approved: Treasury Laws Amendment (Accelerated Depreciation for Small Business Entities) Bill 2018
Treasury Laws Amendment (Accelerated Depreciation for Small Business Entities) Bill 2018 - in Committee - Encourage energy-efficiency

Labor supported the Treasury Laws Amendment (Accelerated Depreciation for Small Business Entities) Bill 2018, which extends the $20,000 instant asset write-off for small businesses for another year at a cost of $350 million, and moved a second reading amendment promoting Labor's alternative Australian Investment Guarantee—a permanent 20 per cent immediate deduction on new investments.

The member for Fairfax argued the Turnbull government was delivering record funding for hospitals and schools and accused Labor of lying and planning $200 billion in new taxes. He supported extending the $20,000 instant asset write-off for small businesses to 30 June 2019, citing over 5,500 businesses in his electorate using it and over 12,700 new jobs created on the Sunshine Coast.

Labor supports the bill to extend the $20,000 instant asset write-off for small businesses for another year, but criticises its temporary nature and the government's repeated short-term extensions. Labor proposes its own permanent Australian Investment Guarantee, allowing all businesses to immediately deduct 20% of new asset investments, citing support from business groups including ACCI, Ai Group, and COSBOA.

The speaker argued in favour of the Treasury Laws Amendment (Accelerated Depreciation for Small Business Entities) Bill 2018, which extends accelerated depreciation rules for small businesses by 12 months to 30 June 2018, including an immediate deduction for assets under a $20,000 threshold for businesses with turnover under $10 million.

The speaker supported the Treasury Laws Amendment Bill, arguing that coalition government policies—including cutting company tax from 48-49% to 30%—have increased company tax receipts as a share of GDP and enabled funding for health programs, while criticising the opposition's amendment and economic record.

The speaker supported extending accelerated depreciation for small businesses with turnover up to $10 million to immediately expense capital purchases up to $20,000, and criticised the opposition for voting against tax relief for businesses with $2 million turnover and for proposing a 50% increase in capital gains tax on all investments. He also noted that 415,000 jobs were created in 2017.

The speaker argued that the Treasury Laws Amendment (Accelerated Depreciation for Small Business Entities) Bill 2018 should be passed, extending the instant asset write-off for businesses with turnover up to $10 million to deduct assets up to $20,000 immediately, and claimed the government’s policies created 420,000 jobs in the past year, with most in businesses up to $50 million turnover that received company tax cuts.
